markdown_content: ## Overview of Knit Swatch Editor in Clo 2025.2 This section introduces the Knit Swatch Editor feature in Clo 2025.2, focusing on how users can create, edit, and visualize knitwear swatches and stitches directly within the software. It highlights the integration of knitwear properties into garment projects and the initial access point for the Knit Swatch Editor. ## Accessing the Knit Swatch Editor To use the Knit Swatch Editor in Clo: - Add knitwear to your project by selecting the fabric with the type set to **Knitwear** in the Object Browser. - Select the knitwear fabric (e.g., "Knit Main Body") under the fabric tab. - In the Property Editor, verify the fabric type is set to Knitwear. - Click the yarn ball icon next to the stitching type; this opens the beta version of the Knit Swatch Editor. This editor allows for easier and more detailed stitch visualization compared to previous versions. --- ## Knit Swatch Editor Interface and Basic Controls This section explains the primary controls and parameters in the Knit Swatch Editor, including swatch dimensions, yarn properties, and gauge settings. ### Swatch Settings - **Wale Amount**: Number of columns in the swatch (horizontal stitch count). - **Courses**: Number of rows in the swatch (vertical stitch count). - **Yarn Thickness**: Diameter of the yarn. - **Gauge**: Needles per inch, affecting stitch density. Hovering over each setting displays a tooltip with explanations. ### Live vs. Non-Live Updates - Changes to **Yarn Thickness** and **Gauge** update live in the swatch preview. - Changes to **Wale Amount** and **Courses** require clicking **Reset Swatch** to apply, which resets the swatch design. ### Reset Swatch Function - Resets all stitch designs to apply new wale and course amounts. - Any stitch edits are lost when resetting, so save changes beforehand. --- ## Gauge Linking and Unlinking for Advanced Control The editor links most options to the gauge setting by default, simplifying design for typical use cases. ### Linked Mode (Default) - Parameters auto-adjust based on the gauge value. - Recommended for general design work or when no physical swatch reference is available. ### Unlinked Mode (Advanced) - Allows manual entry of wales per inch and courses per inch. - Useful for replicating a physical swatch that may have shrunk or been blocked. - Example: Setting 9.5 rows per inch and 15 columns per inch to mimic a real swatch. - Changing these values affects fabric thickness and swatch appearance. ### Switching Between Modes - Toggle linking to switch between design mode and replication mode. - Clicking **Link** reapplies gauge-based automatic sizing. - Remember to click **Reset Swatch** after changing wale and course counts. --- ## Navigation and Viewing Controls in the Knit Swatch Editor The swatch preview window uses 3D navigation controls familiar to Clo users: - **Zoom In/Out**: Middle mouse wheel. - **Pan/Move**: Click and hold middle mouse button, drag. - **Rotate**: Right mouse button drag. - **Preset Views**: Right-click menu or number keys for front, left, right, etc. - **Toggle Menus**: Button to switch yarn display modes such as thick yarn, thin yarn, or random color yarn. --- ## Stitch Editing Tools and Simulation Controls This section details the available stitch manipulation tools and simulation features within the Knit Swatch Editor. ### Stitch Types and Shortcuts - **Front Knit (Q)**: Default stitch type. - **Back Knit (W)** - **Front Miss (E)** - **Back Miss (R)** All shortcuts are located on the left side of a standard English keyboard for easy access. ### Editing Stitches - Click to change a stitch type. - Click and drag to change multiple stitches simultaneously. - Use shortcut keys to quickly switch stitch types. ### Simulation - **Spacebar** toggles simulation on/off. - When simulation is on, stitch adjustments update live. - Best practice: Keep simulation off when making extensive edits for smoother performance. - Simulation visually demonstrates how stitch patterns behave in real knitwear. --- ## Applying Swatches to Garments and Live Updates - Changes made in the Knit Swatch Editor automatically apply to the selected fabric in the 3D garment window. - Adjustments such as yarn thickness and gauge dynamically update the garment appearance upon clicking **Apply**. - Users can toggle simulation post-application to preview knit behavior on the garment in real time. - The editor supports continuous editing by reopening and adjusting swatches without losing prior settings. --- ## Creating and Managing Custom Knit Swatch Presets - Users can save custom knit swatch configurations as presets for reuse. - Saving captures stitch patterns, yarn thickness, gauge, and color settings. - Presets allow for quick application of favorite or standard knit patterns across projects. - If a swatch is reset or lost, saved presets can be reopened to restore all prior data. --- ## Troubleshooting Stitch Distortion and Resetting Linking - Stitch distortion can occur if gauge linking is disabled improperly. - Unlinked wale and course per inch values may cause unwanted stretch or elongation in stitches. - To fix distortion: 1. Reopen the Knit Swatch Editor. 2. Ensure the **Link** option for gauge is enabled. 3. Click **Apply** and **Close** to update the garment swatch. - This relinks parameters to the gauge and normalizes stitch proportions. - Keeping gauge linked is recommended unless precise physical swatch replication is needed. --- ## Color Variants and Batch Editing - The editor supports changing yarn colors directly within the swatch. - Multiple stitches or yarn sections can be selected simultaneously (using Shift key) for batch color updates. - This feature streamlines creating variant color options for knit fabrics. --- ## Summary The Knit Swatch Editor in Clo 2025.2 introduces robust tools for knitwear design, allowing detailed stitch editing, live simulation, custom preset creation, and precise control over knitwear parameters such as wale and course counts, yarn thickness, and gauge. Navigation mimics Clo’s 3D environment controls, and keyboard shortcuts enable efficient workflow. Users should be mindful of the distinction between linked and unlinked gauge modes, especially to avoid stitch distortion. The editor integrates seamlessly with garment previews, providing dynamic updates to fabric appearance. This beta feature is expected to evolve with future improvements.

Users should be mindful of the distinction between linked and unlinked gauge modes, especially to avoid stitch distortion. The editor integrates seamlessly with garment previews, providing dynamic updates to fabric appearance. This beta feature is expected to evolve with future improvements.
